idle.note: Per-direction static rotation frame (the 8-dir rotation set, no animation generated).

source.notes: Exploratory pass from the second human concept reference (heavyset build). Output canvas is 68x68 square, NOT the approved 64x80 Hunter canvas - reconciliation is Stage 3 (Aseprite) work. Deliberately kept outside apps/ : not wired to the client.

measurements.note: Height sits inside the approved range (better than build A's 52-54). Width 24px on n/s against build A's 20px - the extra mass reads front and back, but only 17px on e/w.

driftFromBrief: The heavy build reads clearly on n/s/ne/se/sw/nw but the pure side views (e, w) are 17px wide and read closer to average - the belly silhouette is largely lost in profile.
Hood is worn UP in all 8 directions; both references have it down with the face and beard visible. Same drift as build A.
The beard is not legible at 48px; the face reads as a light skin mass.
Belt pouch, shoulder strap and forearm tattoos are not resolvable at this scale (expected).
The cream tunic reads as a bright front panel, which pulls attention to the torso more than the reference does.

comparison.note: Same wardrobe language and palette drift (green brighter than the proposed moss family). Build B wins on height compliance and on carrying the belt pouch + shoulder strap that visual-direction.md asks for; build A wins on profile-view silhouette consistency.
